output.contract_title: Master Services Agreement (MSA) with Enterprise Partner 018 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Vendor shall notify Customer in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach.
Each party's maximum aggregate liability shall be strictly limited to the total fees paid under this Agreement in the preceding twelve (12) months.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive two-year periods and CANNOT be terminated for convenience prior to full term expiration.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Aggregate liability cap must not exceed 12 months of total fees paid or payable.
Customer must have the right to terminate for convenience with no more than 30 days prior written notice.

ambiguities_in_policy.issue: Definition of "total fees paid or payable" is not specified (e.g., includes recurring fees, one‑time fees, taxes, discounts?).
Method and acceptable format for the "written notice" (email, postal mail, electronic portal) are not defined.

mappings.notes: Liability cap exactly matches the 12‑month fee limitation.
Provides customer (and both parties) a 30‑day convenience termination right, meeting the requirement.
Prohibits termination for convenience before term end, directly contradicting the required 30‑day convenience termination right.

deviations.supporting_evidence: Clause CLS-0018-REN prohibits termination for convenience before the term ends, directly contradicting the policy requirement that the customer must have a 30‑day prior written notice right to terminate for convenience.
deviations.recommended_remediation: Amend or remove clause CLS-0018-REN so that the contract grants the customer a unilateral right to terminate for convenience with at least 30 days written notice, aligning the termination provisions with REQ-LGL-02.

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The term "undisputed invoice amounts" is not defined, leaving uncertainty about which invoices are payable within 30 days and potentially causing payment delays.
"Confirmed Data Breach" is not defined, making it unclear when the vendor's 24‑hour notification obligation is triggered.
Limiting aggregate liability to fees paid in the preceding twelve months may be insufficient to cover certain damages, especially third‑party claims, exposing the customer to uncovered risk.

The termination‑for‑convenience provision (30‑day notice) conflicts with the renewal clause that prohibits termination for convenience before the full term, creating enforceability and operational uncertainty.
Automatic renewal for successive two‑year periods with a prohibition on termination for convenience locks the customer into long terms without flexibility.
No notice period is specified for opting out of the automatic renewal, leaving the customer without a clear mechanism to prevent unintended extensions.

inconsistencies.description: Clause CLS-0018-TERM permits either party to terminate the Agreement for convenience with 30 days' written notice, while Clause CLS-0018-REN states the Agreement cannot be terminated for convenience prior to the full term expiration and automatically renews for successive two‑year periods. These provisions directly conflict regarding the right to terminate for convenience.

The Term clause defines the initial term as one year (2026‑01‑01 to 2027‑01‑01), but the Renewal clause specifies automatic renewal for successive two‑year periods. The renewal period length is inconsistent with the defined initial term length, creating a chronological mismatch.

How is a "confirmed Data Breach" determined under this agreement?
Is there an exception or supplemental cap for third‑party claims or statutory damages?
Can the renewal clause be amended to include an opt‑out notice period that aligns with the 30‑day convenience termination right?

recommended_actions.description: Amend or remove clause CLS-0018-REN so that the contract grants the customer a unilateral right to terminate for convenience with at least 30 days written notice, aligning with REQ-LGL-02.
Define "undisputed invoice amounts" in the payment terms to eliminate ambiguity and reduce payment‑delay risk.
Provide a clear definition of "confirmed Data Breach" and outline the verification process for the vendor.
